title: Git MCP Server
summary: Give your agent structured git tools for status, diffs, logs, branches and commits through the reference mcp-server-git, fenced to one repository.
description: mcp-server-git is the reference Git server from the Model Context Protocol project. It exposes tools such as git_status, git_diff, git_log, git_show, git_branch and git_commit, so an agent can inspect and stage work without shelling out.
It runs locally through uvx and needs no account. The --repository flag confines it to the working tree you name, which is worth setting so the agent cannot wander into other clones on the disk.
useWhen: Ask what changed since the last release tag
Have the agent draft a commit message from the staged diff
Compare a feature branch with main before opening a pull request
Find which commit touched a file in the last two weeks

mcp.name: git
access: Reads status, diffs, history and branches of the repository you point it at
Can stage files, commit, create branches, check out and merge (fast-forward only by default)

example.prompt: Show the staged diff and write a one-line commit message in the imperative.
example.result: Staged: 3 files, +42 -7, all in src/billing. Suggested message: "Round invoice totals before applying tax". Nothing was committed.

faq.question: Do I need Python installed?
faq.answer: You need uv, which provides uvx. It fetches mcp-server-git on first run. Git 2.31 or newer must be on the PATH.

faq.question: Can it push to a remote?
faq.answer: The tool list has no push. It lists remotes with credentials hidden, and commits stay local until you push yourself.

faq.question: Why keep the --repository flag?
faq.answer: Without it the server can act on any repository it can reach. Pinning it to the current folder limits what a bad prompt can touch.

access: Local git repository: reads history, writes commits and branches
No network calls of its own
